[b]NORRHOLLOW DEPARTMENT OF WAR
HEADQUARTERS
AFTER-ACTION REVIEW
FORT BLACKHURST[/b]

[b]AESIR-VTR-OPS [/b]
[b]CO [/b]██████
[b]DATE: [/b]█████████

[b]MEMORANDUM FOR[/b]: CPT. Vivian A. Ravnskald, DOW ATTN: OCD-AA 5 Ord Road, Building 12C Fort Blackhurst NW

[b]SUBJECT[/b]: Operation STILL TIDE, After Action Report

[b]I. MISSION OBJECTIVES.[/b]

[list=1]

[*]Establish military presence over GR: 3406 "FOB Still Tide" (island later renamed Austmark).

[*]Conduct terrain assessment and fortification efforts.

[*]Coordinate Task Force 5 "Trojan" and 1st Battalion "Lightfoot", 205th Armored Infantry Regiment strategic objectives; operate as vanguard force.

[*]Monitor coastal activity for unauthorized incursions.

[*]ROE: Strictly non-aggressive; primary focus on reconnaissance, fortification, and logistics. 

[/list]

[b]II. OP. STILL TIDE CHRONOLOGY[/b]

[list]PHASE 1: INITIAL LANDING

[LIST]

[i]0400 Hours[/i] -  Task Force 5 deploys via rotary-wing insertion. No resistance encountered.

[list]

[b]Trojan 6 (RAVNSKALD)[/b]: "Lightfoot 6, this is Trojan 6, message over."

[b]Lightfoot 6 (MORRISON)[/b]: "Trojan 6, this is Lightfoot 6, send message over."

[b]Trojan 6[/b]: "Trojan elements are wheels down, securing the LZ. No resistance. Your element is clear to begin offloading, over.

[b]Lightfoot 6[/b]: "Roger, Trojan 6. Lightfoot elements inboard. ETA, fifteen mikes. Alpha Company's apparently already on the ridge so we're gonna have to shuffle, out."

[/list]

1st Battalion follows via amphibious landing craft. Offloading logistics commence with Task Force 5 reconnaissance elements secure high-ground observation points. 

[list]

[b]Trojan 6[/b]: "1-4 this is Trojan 6 Actual, how's the situation, over."

[b]Trojan 1-4 (ARNTZEN)[/b]: "Trojan 6, 1-4. We've conducted overwatch on the ridge but no heat signatures, no hostiles. Terrain is safe for construction, recommending primary FOB at Grid 3406."

[b]Trojan 6[/b]: "Copy that, 1-4. Relaying to Lightfoot. Lightfoot 6, your call on the FOB site?"

[b]Lightfoot 6[/b]: "Trojan 6, this is Lightfoot 6. Grid 3406 is acceptable, our elements are bringing in supplies. Bravo and Delta should be starting on the earthworks an hour from now, out."

[/list]

[/list]

PHASE 2: PERIMETER SECURITY AND FORTIFICATION

[list]

[i]0600 Hours - 1st Battalion engineers deploy concertina wire and prefabricated structures. Task Force 5 maintains outer security/[/i]

[list]

[b]Trojan 3-3 (COLDING)[/b]: "Trojan 6, this is 3-3. Southern perimeter has been established. Lightfoot engineers are laying down concertina wire now, over."

[b]Trojan 6[/b]: "Acknowledged, 3-3. Lightfoot 6, do you copy?"

[b]Lightfoot 6[/b]: "Loud and clear, Trojan 6. Our patrols will maintain a presence. Do you recommend additional checkpoints?"

[b]Trojan 6[/b]: "Affirmative, Lightfoot 6. We recommend a second elevated OP at the northern cliffs in case Venny feels like doing something that'll need visibility."

[b]Lightfoot 6[/b]: "Roger, Trojan 6. We'll deploy a squad to establish an observation post there."

[/list]

Whole perimeter of FOB Still Tide secured by 0700 Hours. No external activity detected. Operational tempo remained steady for duration of occupation.

[/list]

PHASE 3: UNIDENTIFIED STRUCTURE AT GRID 3275

[list]

[i]0715 Hours [/i]- Unidentified structure discovered built into the northern ridge of FOB Still Tide at Grid 3275. 

[list]

[b]Delta 1-3 (HOYER)[/b]: "Uh... Lightfoot 6, this is Delta 1-3, message over."

[b]Lightfoot 6[/b]: "Delta 1-3, this is Lightfoot 6, send message over."

[b]Delta 1-3[/b]: "There's a structure at Grid 3275. Looks like an abandoned station, requesting directives, over."

[b]Lightfoot 6[/b]: "Hold tight, Delta 1-3. Trojan 6 this is Lightfoot 6, we've discovered what appears to be er... an abandoned station at Grid 3275. Marking it as SITE 3275. Are your engineers on top of it? Over."

[b]Trojan 6[/b]: "Copy that, Lightfoot 6. My guys will take a closer look. Have an ISTAR team en route to SITE 3275."

[b]Lightfoot 6[/b]: "Roger, Trojan 6, sending Delta Company's ISTAR ETA five minutes. Out."

[/list]

Upon inspection, SITE 3275 (later ascribed "UNIDENT-01" in later briefings) appears to have been constructed from ballistic concrete, some amorphous fiberglass, and possessing several tons of electronics, was in a state of abandon and disrepair at the time of discovery, no life signs detected after rigorous investigation, concluded to have possibly been an abandoned weather station or relay.

[/list]

[b]III. OBSERVATIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS[/b]

[list=1]

[*]FOB Still Tide presents limited natural defenses but permits rapid fortification, advise to avoid further developments near the western reef where waves are most violent.

[*]Further developments should be made at the northern ridge preempting potential disruptions from Thyven and other foreign actors. Additionally, increased UAV patrols and potential naval presence for deterrence.

[*]UNIDENT-01 should be placed under military-civilian administration until it is deemed to be fully safe to access.

[*]1st Battalion, 205th Armored Infantry Regiment performed their rapid deployment efficiently. Task Force 5 reconnaissance ensured optimal defensive positioning.

[/list]

[b]IV. RENAMING AND PERMANENT PRESENCE[/b]

[list]Following its successful occupation, FOB Still Tide was officially renamed "Austmark Island" as per the direction of the Department of War and the Land Commission. Future missions shall refer to the area as "Austmark" or "Austmark Island" in all communications.[/list]

[b]V. CONCLUSION[/b]

[list]Operation STILL TIDE met all strategic objectives. CAUSE and NSR forces displayed a high degree of cohesion, established effective coordination, and sustained logistical operations. Presence on Austmark Island shall be maintained until further notice.[/list]

[b]VI. CLASSIFICATION AND DISTRIBUTION[/b]

[list]

Classification: ████████

Authorized Recipients: ████████████

[/list]

[u][b]END OF REPORT[/b][/u]

[b]OF ANGELS AND MORTALS[/b]
[i]1: Kuro Hizumi[/i]

STARBOUND: 2500]
[i]At the age of 14, Kuro Hizumi lives alone.

He doesn't hate being alone. He has no reason to hate being alone. He doesn't desire for relationships of any kind, given the only two he ever really had left him behind at a young age.

Kuro doesn't know much about his parents. He only knows that his father and mother work for the League of Eiridia, and that neither of them have any time to raise their only son.

To Kuro, his parents are dead.

Kuro has many different reasons to despise others. Above all, he despises being intimate. His hatred of others has led to him becoming what many Makinese people call a 'hikikomori.'

He is a shut-in.

Kuro is not interested in the world, and as far as he knows, the world is not interested in him.

Just as things should be.[/i]

...

[i]Burokuo City, Northern Makina[/i]
Kuro wakes up to the sounds of birds chirping outside his apartment window. Within the husk of Burokuo City, the only sound ever heard in the morning are the sounds of birds and the sounds of waves sloshing around on the flooded streets below. Like many coastal cities in Makina, Burokuo is half-submerged in the waters of the Great Ocean. It is a miracle alone that people can still live in such conditions, but due to the shabby state of affairs in the country it isn't much of a surprise that many have had to make do with their less-than-favourable living arrangements.

Kuro climbs out of his bed, and begins to start his daily routine.

Stretch. Go to the shower. Clean up. Brush his fur. Brush his teeth. Go to the kitchen. Make food.

Every morning, Kuro's day-to-day life begins like this. He is comfortable with this routine, no matter how boring or repetitive it gets.

His food is canned meat. He knows how the Makinese government produces this particular ration - from the bodies of dead Kane. While his neighbours tend to eschew the canned meat based on this knowledge, he doesn't.

Kuro could give a fu*k that his food used to be alive, just like him. In the world of the Second Awakening, you must make do with what you have. And regardless of where the meat came from, it is a good source of nutrients and a great way to survive one more day in this hellish planet.

Kuro sits down at the dining table in his apartment. In older times, this table was the place where the Hizumi family would gather to talk about their plans for the day. The environment used to be happy and cheery. Kuro and his parents used to enjoy being in the company of one another. They wouldn't give a fu*k about the canned meat; all of them would happily eat it and move on with their life.

Now, there is no more Mr. or Mrs. Hizumi. Both of them are out of his life. Kuro's table is sad, depressing and lonely, just like the rest of his apartment.

And Kuro doesn't care.

He is about halfway done with his can when he suddenly hears a knock on the door. He is taken aback by this, and stares at his door in confusion. 

Nobody had ever tried to bother him before. Why now?

He heads over to his door cautiously and peeps through the fish hole.

It's a mailman.

[i]"Hello? Anyone home? I have a letter for a... uh... Huro- no, Kuro Hizumi?"[/i]

Kuro tentatively opens the door.

"Uh, hi. I'll take the letter, thank you."

The mailman passes Kuro the letter, and wishes him well before moving on. As the mailman walks away, he stares down at the letter in his hands.

It's a letter from the League of Eiridia. He can tell, since the envelope is marked with the insignia of the organisation. There is also another symbol on it; a blood-red logo that reads "RION."

Kuro closes the door and walks back into his apartment to read this letter.

...

[i]To Kuro Hizumi,

Your services have been requested by Commander Hizumi at RION headquarters in the capital of Ayana-2. Please come to Ayana-2 within 4 days of receiving this notice.

A transport will be provided for you once you arrive in Ayana-2. Call 0-555-394-404 to hail for the transport.

From,
RION Headquarters
Ayana-2
Southern Makina[/i]

...

Kuro doesn't know how to take this letter. After all this time, his father has finally reached out to him.

And for what?

Why?

Why does his father want to see him now?

Kuro's feelings boil over into pure fury. He is angry at his dad, and how self-absorbed and obnoxious and toxic and... and... 

Kuro begins to cry. He throws the letter in the bin, and then storms back to his bed to think this all through. He shoves his pillow over his head and continues to quietly sob.

For the first time in a long time, Kuro's daily routine was finally broken.

The birds are still chirping.
[/spoiler]
